title: Integrability of the weighted Gaussian density Hessian
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f(z)|\le 1$ for every $z$, let $v>0$, and let $c\in\mathbb R^I$. Define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$. The function sending $z$ to $f(z)$ times the bilinear form $(h,k)\mapsto G_v(c,z)\bigl(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v\bigr)$ is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^I$, as a bilinear-form-valued function.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Put $G_v(c,z)=\prod_i p_v(c_i,z_i)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density of variance $v$ for $v>0$ and $p_0=0$, and put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$, with division by zero equal to zero. Define $A_v(c,z)[h]=G_v(c,z)S_v(c,z)[h]$ and $T_v(c,z)[h,k]=G_v(c,z)(S_v(c,z)[h]S_v(c,z)[k]-\sum_i h_i k_i/v)$. Let $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ be measurable with $|f|\le1$. If $v>0$ and $c\in\mathbb R^I$, then $z\mapsto f(z)T_v(c,z)$ is Lebesgue-integrable as a bilinear-form-valued function.
